title: BEGIN...END Statement
description: Learn how to use BEGIN...END to group Transact-SQL statements into a block.

data.text: The BEGIN...END statement defines a statement block — a set of SQL statements that execute together. Think of it as defining a paragraph of code.

data.title: Basic BEGIN...END syntax
data.content: Groups multiple statements into a single block.

data.title: BEGIN...END with IF statement
data.content: Uses BEGIN...END to group statements inside an IF block.
data.code:
BEGIN
    DECLARE @name VARCHAR(MAX);

    SELECT TOP 1
        @name = product_name
    FROM
        production.products
    ORDER BY
        list_price DESC;

    IF @@ROWCOUNT <> 0
    BEGIN
        PRINT 'The most expensive product is ' + @name
    END
    ELSE
    BEGIN
        PRINT 'No product found';
    END;
END

data.title: BEGIN...END Key Points
points: BEGIN...END groups statements into a logical block.
Required for IF...ELSE, WHILE, and other control-of-flow statements.
Blocks can be nested inside other blocks.
Often used at the start and end of stored procedures and functions.
